# internet-ui full registry

> Complete component catalog for coding agents and other LLM clients.

Initialize a target project before adding components:

```bash
npx @ternetin/ui init
npx @ternetin/ui add <component...>
```

The CLI resolves registry dependencies, rewrites `@/lib/*` and `@/ui/*` imports to target aliases, installs npm dependencies, and writes editable local source.

## Theme (`theme`)

internet-ui design tokens (Tailwind v4). Import once from your global stylesheet.

- Type: `registry:style`
- Install: `npx @ternetin/ui add theme`
- npm dependencies: `tailwindcss@^4.3.3`, `tw-animate-css@^1.4.0`
- Registry dependencies: none

### `src/theme/globals.css`

````css
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "tw-animate-css";

@custom-variant dark (&:is(.dark *));

/*
 * internet-ui — design tokens
 * Shared application foundations. Public pages opt into expressive display
 * typography; application components share fixed geometry and quiet surfaces.
 */
:root {
  color-scheme: light;
  --background: #f8fafc;
  --foreground: #0b1020;

  --card: #ffffff;
  --card-foreground: #0b1020;
  --popover: #ffffff;
  --popover-foreground: #0b1020;

  --primary: #0047ff;
  --primary-foreground: #ffffff;

  --secondary: #f6f8fb;
  --secondary-foreground: #111827;

  --muted: #f3f6fb;
  --muted-foreground: #5f6b7a;

  --accent: #eef4ff;
  --accent-foreground: #0038cc;

  --destructive: #b91c1c;
  --destructive-foreground: #ffffff;

  --success: #0f7b4f;
  --success-foreground: #ffffff;
  --success-muted: #e8f7ef;

  --warning: #b45309;
  --warning-foreground: #ffffff;
  --warning-muted: #fff4dc;

  --info: #0f5bd8;
  --info-foreground: #ffffff;
  --info-muted: #eaf2ff;

  /*
   * Hairline borders, not black rules. Translucent so a border tints toward
   * whatever surface it sits on (card, muted, an image) instead of stamping a
   * fixed grey over it. Text and accents carry the contrast; edges only imply it.
   */
  --border: rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.14);
  --input: #8592a3;
  --ring: #0047ff;
  --shadow-color: rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.16);

  /*
   * Syntax colours, used only inside a highlighted Code block. Three inks and no
   * more: the house blue for language keywords, a violet for names, a green for
   * literals. Comments and punctuation borrow --muted-foreground, and everything
   * else stays --foreground, so a snippet still reads as page text with accents
   * rather than as a rainbow.
   */
  --syntax-keyword: #0047ff;
  --syntax-name: #6d28d9;
  --syntax-literal: #047857;

  --control-radius: 0.375rem;
  --surface-radius: 0.5rem;
  --radius: var(--control-radius);
  --elevation-popup: 0 4px 16px rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.12);
  --elevation-modal: 0 16px 48px rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.18);

  --font-sans: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif;
  --font-mono: "SFMono-Regular", "Cascadia Code", "Liberation Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace;
}

@theme inline {
  --color-background: var(--background);
  --color-foreground: var(--foreground);

  --color-primary: var(--primary);
  --color-primary-foreground: var(--primary-foreground);
  --color-secondary: var(--secondary);
  --color-secondary-foreground: var(--secondary-foreground);
  --color-muted: var(--muted);
  --color-muted-foreground: var(--muted-foreground);
  --color-accent: var(--accent);
  --color-accent-foreground: var(--accent-foreground);
  --color-destructive: var(--destructive);
  --color-destructive-foreground: var(--destructive-foreground);
  --color-success: var(--success);
  --color-success-foreground: var(--success-foreground);
  --color-success-muted: var(--success-muted);
  --color-warning: var(--warning);
  --color-warning-foreground: var(--warning-foreground);
  --color-warning-muted: var(--warning-muted);
  --color-info: var(--info);
  --color-info-foreground: var(--info-foreground);
  --color-info-muted: var(--info-muted);
  --color-border: var(--border);
  --color-input: var(--input);
  --color-ring: var(--ring);
  --color-syntax-keyword: var(--syntax-keyword);
  --color-syntax-name: var(--syntax-name);
  --color-syntax-literal: var(--syntax-literal);

  --font-sans: var(--font-sans);
  --font-mono: var(--font-mono);

  --radius-control: var(--control-radius);

  --radius-md: var(--control-radius);

/* Structural seams take precedence over the child control radius utilities. */
.ui-input-group > :not(:last-child) {
  border-start-end-radius: 0;
  border-end-end-radius: 0;
}

  }

## cn utility (`utils`)

Shared clsx/tailwind-merge utility and fixed nested-popup geometry.

- Type: `registry:lib`
- Install: `npx @ternetin/ui add utils`
- npm dependencies: `clsx@^2.1.1`, `tailwind-merge@^3.7.0`
- Registry dependencies: none

### `src/lib/utils.ts`

````ts
import { type ClassValue, clsx } from 'clsx';
import { twMerge } from 'tailwind-merge';

export function cn(...inputs: ClassValue[]) {
  return twMerge(clsx(inputs));
}

/** Fixed inner corner for an item inside a padded popup. */
export const NESTED_RADIUS = 'rounded-[calc(var(--surface-radius)-0.25rem)]';
````

## Motion presets (`motion`)

Shared animation language: easing curves, duration and spring tokens, and the render-prop helpers that animate Base UI popups with Motion.

- Type: `registry:lib`
- Install: `npx @ternetin/ui add motion`
- npm dependencies: `motion@^12.43.0`
- Registry dependencies: none

### `src/lib/motion.tsx`

````tsx
'use client';

import { type HTMLMotionProps, motion, type Transition, useReducedMotion, type Variants } from 'motion/react';
import * as React from 'react';

/**
 * Shared motion language for internet-ui.
 *
 * Every component here is still a Base UI component: Motion is applied through
 * Base UI's `render` prop, so the primitive keeps its behaviour, accessibility and
 * state attributes, and only gains an animated element to render into.
 *
 * The house style is crisp, not bouncy: short ease-out curves for surfaces that
 * appear, springs reserved for controls the user toggles or drags. Sharp corners
 * and Helvetica don't want overshoot.
 *
 * HOW POPUP EXIT ANIMATIONS WORK — read this before changing anything here.
 *
 * Base UI unmounts a closed popup only once `element.getAnimations()` reports
 * nothing running. That one behaviour is what lets these components animate out
 * while staying uncontrolled — no `AnimatePresence`, no `keepMounted`, and no
 * `open` state lifted into the consumer's component. Two rules fall out of it:
 *
 *  1. Every exit animation must include `opacity`. It's the property Base UI can
 *     reliably see, because Motion drives it through the Web Animations API. A
 *     transform-only or height-only animation is invisible to that check, and the
 *     element gets torn out of the DOM on the frame it starts leaving.
 *  2. Popups use duration-based tweens, never springs. Springs settle
 *     asymptotically, so `getAnimations()` stays non-empty for ~250ms after a
 *     spring *looks* done — leaving an invisible popup mounted, still holding its
 *     focus scope. Springs are free to use anywhere that stays mounted.
 *
 * WHAT DELIBERATELY ISN'T HERE
 *
 * A few parts animate in CSS instead, and not for lack of trying:
 *
 *  - Accordion and Collapsible panels. Base UI tears an in-flow panel out of the
 *    DOM as soon as its CSS transition ends, and checks for one earlier than
 *    Motion — which starts animating in an effect after paint — can register. A
 *    Motion panel expands correctly and then vanishes instead of collapsing.
 *  - Drawer and Toast. Both implement swipe gestures by publishing the pointer
 *    delta as CSS variables and expecting `transform` to be composed from them.
 *    A `motion.div` owns `transform`, so the sheet would stop tracking the finger.
 *  - The Tabs indicator, and Progress/Meter fills. Their target geometry arrives
 *    as a CSS variable or an inline style. Motion can't re-run an animation when
 *    the value behind a `var()` changes, because the target string it compares
 *    never changes.
 *
 * Each of those files says so at the point of use.
 */

/** Cubic-bezier curves used across the library. */
export const easings = {
  /** Decelerate hard. Default for anything entering. */
  out: [0.22, 1, 0.36, 1],
  /**
   * Accelerate away. Default for anything leaving. Kept mild on purpose — a
   * steeper ease-in barely moves for the first half of a 150ms exit, which reads
   * as the popup hesitating before it closes.
   */
  in: [0.4, 0, 1, 1],
  /** Symmetric. For size and position changes on things already on screen. */
  inOut: [0.32, 0.72, 0, 1]
} as const satisfies Record<string, [number, number, number, number]>;

/** Seconds. Deliberately short — this library should feel immediate. */
export const durations = {
  instant: 0.1,
  fast: 0.15,
  base: 0.2,
  slow: 0.28
} as const;

export const transitions = {
  /** A surface appearing: popovers, menus, dialogs, tooltips. */
  enter: { duration: durations.base, ease: easings.out },
  /** The same surface leaving. Quicker than entering — get out of the way. */
  exit: { duration: durations.fast, ease: easings.in },
  /** Opacity-only crossfades: backdrops, indicators, text swaps. */
  fade: { duration: durations.fast, ease: 'linear' },
  /** Height and width changes: accordion and collapsible panels. */
  size: { duration: durations.slow, ease: easings.inOut },
  /** Toggle controls that stay mounted: switch thumb, checkbox tick. */
  control: { type: 'spring', stiffness: 700, damping: 32, mass: 0.5 },
  /** Indicators that travel between siblings: tabs, toggle groups. */
  indicator: { type: 'spring', stiffness: 550, damping: 42, mass: 0.9 },
  /** Larger surfaces sliding into place: toasts. */
  surface: { type: 'spring', stiffness: 420, damping: 38, mass: 0.9 }
} as const satisfies Record<string, Transition>;

/**
 * Minimal shape of the state Base UI passes to a `render` callback. `side` is
 * typed loosely so this stays assignable to every component's own state type.
 */
export interface PopupMotionState {
  open: boolean;
  side?: string;
}

export interface PopupMotionOptions {
  /**
   * Scale the surface grows from. `1` opts out of scaling.
   * @default 0.96
   */
  scale?: number;
  /**
   * Distance in px the surface travels toward its anchor as it appears. The
   * direction comes from the `side` the positioner reports, so a popup anchored
   * below its trigger slides down into place.
   * @default 4
   */
  offset?: number;
  /** Overrides the enter transition. */
  transition?: Transition;
  /** Overrides the exit transition. */
  exitTransition?: Transition;
}

/** Motion props derived from a Base UI open state. */
export interface StateMotionProps {
  initial: string;
  animate: string;
  variants: Variants;
}

function offsetFor(side: string | undefined, offset: number) {
  switch (side) {
    case 'top':
      return { y: offset };
    case 'bottom':
      return { y: -offset };
    case 'left':
    case 'inline-start':
      return { x: offset };
    case 'right':
    case 'inline-end':
      return { x: -offset };
    default:
      return {};
  }
}

/**
 * Enter/exit animation for a popup surface, driven by Base UI's open state.
 *
 * Prefer {@link useMotionPopupRender}, which wires this into a `render` prop.
 * Reach for this hook directly when a popup needs extra motion props of its own.
 *
 * Honours `prefers-reduced-motion` by collapsing to a plain crossfade — which
 * keeps unmount deferral intact, since opacity is still animated.
 */
export function usePopupMotion(options: PopupMotionOptions = {}) {
  const { scale = 0.96, offset = 4, transition = transitions.enter, exitTransition = transitions.exit } = options;
  const reduceMotion = useReducedMotion();

  return React.useCallback(
    (state: PopupMotionState): StateMotionProps => ({
      initial: 'closed',
      animate: state.open ? 'open' : 'closed',
      variants: {
        closed: reduceMotion
          ? { opacity: 0, transition: exitTransition }
          : { opacity: 0, scale, ...offsetFor(state.side, offset), transition: exitTransition },
        open: { opacity: 1, scale: 1, x: 0, y: 0, transition }
      }
    }),
    [reduceMotion, scale, offset, transition, exitTransition]
  );
}

/**
 * `render` prop that animates a popup surface in and out.
 *
 * ```tsx
 * const renderPopup = useMotionPopupRender();
 * return <Popover.Popup render={renderPopup} className="..." />;
 * ```
 */
export function useMotionPopupRender(options?: PopupMotionOptions) {
  const popupMotion = usePopupMotion(options);

  return React.useCallback(
    (props: React.HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>, state: PopupMotionState) => (
      <motion.div {...(props as HTMLMotionProps<'div'>)} {...popupMotion(state)} />
    ),
    [popupMotion]
  );
}

/**
 * `render` prop for backdrops and scrims, where scaling or sliding would be
 * wrong and only a crossfade is wanted.
 */
export function useMotionBackdropRender(transition: Transition = transitions.fade) {
  const backdropMotion = React.useCallback(
    (state: { open: boolean }): StateMotionProps => ({
      initial: 'closed',
      animate: state.open ? 'open' : 'closed',
      variants: {
        closed: { opacity: 0, transition },
        open: { opacity: 1, transition }
      }
    }),
    [transition]
  );

  return React.useCallback(
    (props: React.HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>, state: { open: boolean }) => (
      <motion.div {...(props as HTMLMotionProps<'div'>)} {...backdropMotion(state)} />
    ),
    [backdropMotion]
  );
}

/**
 * Press feedback for buttons and other pressable controls.
 *
 * Returns props for a `motion` element. Disabled entirely under reduced motion —
 * a scale on press is exactly the kind of movement that setting asks us to drop.
 */
export function useTapMotion(scale = 0.97) {
  const reduceMotion = useReducedMotion();

  return React.useMemo(
    () =>
      reduceMotion
        ? {}
        : {
            whileTap: { scale },
            transition: { duration: durations.instant, ease: easings.out } satisfies Transition
          },
    [reduceMotion, scale]
  );
}

/**
 * Spring config for a control that stays mounted, softened to a quick fade when
 * the user asks for reduced motion.
 */
export function useControlTransition(transition: Transition = transitions.control): Transition {
  const reduceMotion = useReducedMotion();
  return reduceMotion ? transitions.fade : transition;
}
````

## Syntax highlighter (`highlight`)

Dependency-free tokenizer behind the Code component's language prop. Shell, JS/TS/JSX, JSON, CSS and HTML.

- Type: `registry:lib`
- Install: `npx @ternetin/ui add highlight`
- npm dependencies: none
- Registry dependencies: none

### `src/lib/highlight.ts`

````ts
/**
 * Tiny syntax highlighter for the Code component.
 *
 * Deliberately not a parser. It scans left to right and takes the first rule that
 * matches at the cursor, which is enough for the snippets a docs page shows — an
 * install command, an import, a config object. Long or unusual code will come out
 * subtly wrong in places, and that's the trade for shipping zero dependencies
 * instead of pulling a grammar-based highlighter into a copy-paste component.
 *
 * The token stream is lossless: joining every `value` back together reproduces the
 * input exactly. That's what lets the copy button keep reading the rendered text.
 */

export type TokenKind = 'plain' | 'comment' | 'keyword' | 'literal' | 'name' | 'punctuation';

export interface Token {
  kind: TokenKind;
  value: string;
  /** Character offset in the source. Unique per token, so it keys rendered spans. */
  start: number;
}

/** Languages the `language` prop accepts. Aliases resolve onto a shared ruleset. */
export type Language =
  | 'shell'
  | 'bash'
  | 'sh'
  | 'zsh'
  | 'console'
  | 'js'
  | 'javascript'
  | 'jsx'
  | 'ts'
  | 'typescript'
  | 'tsx'
  | 'json'
  | 'css'
  | 'html';

interface Cursor {
  /** Character before the cursor; `undefined` at the start of the snippet. */
  previous: string | undefined;
  /** True when only whitespace stands between the cursor and the start of its line. */
  atLineStart: boolean;
}

interface Rule {
  kind: Exclude<TokenKind, 'plain'>;
  /**
   * Must carry the sticky flag. The scanner sets `lastIndex` and matches *at* the
   * cursor rather than searching ahead of it, so rule order decides precedence.
   */
  pattern: RegExp;
  /** Extra condition on where a match may start. */
  where?: (cursor: Cursor) => boolean;
}

/** Not in the middle of a word — keeps `1` in `h1` from reading as a number. */
const notInWord = ({ previous }: Cursor) => previous === undefined || !/[\w$]/.test(previous);

/** Preceded by whitespace — a shell flag or comment starts its own word. */
const afterSpace = ({ previous }: Cursor) => previous === undefined || /\s/.test(previous);

/**
 * Somewhere a JSX tag could legally open. Without this, the `<` of `a<b` reads as
 * the start of a `<b>` element.
 */
const beforeTag = ({ previous }: Cursor) => previous === undefined || /[\s([{},;=>:&|!?+]/.test(previous);

/** Shared by js, ts, jsx and tsx — the differences don't survive this level of detail. */
const JS_RULES: Rule[] = [
  { kind: 'comment', pattern: /\/\/[^\n]*|\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//y },
  { kind: 'literal', pattern: /'(?:[^'\\\n]|\\.)*'|"(?:[^"\\\n]|\\.)*"|`(?:[^`\\]|\\.)*`/y },
  {
    kind: 'keyword',
    pattern:
      /\b(?:as|async|await|break|case|catch|class|const|continue|default|delete|do|else|enum|export|extends|finally|for|from|function|if|implements|import|in|instanceof|interface|let|new|of|private|protected|public|readonly|return|satisfies|static|switch|this|throw|try|type|typeof|var|void|while|yield)\b/y
  },
  { kind: 'literal', pattern: /\b(?:true|false|null|undefined|NaN|Infinity)\b/y },
  { kind: 'name', pattern: /<\/?[A-Za-z][\w.:-]*/y, where: beforeTag },
  { kind: 'literal', pattern: /0[xX][\da-fA-F]+|\d+(?:\.\d+)?(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?/y, where: notInWord },
  // A call, then anything else in PascalCase: components, classes, types.
  { kind: 'name', pattern: /[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*(?=\s*\()/y, where: notInWord },
  { kind: 'name', pattern: /[A-Z][\w$]*/y, where: notInWord },
  // Angle brackets are matched one at a time, and last. Folded into the run above
  // they'd swallow the `<` of `}</Code>` before the tag rule ever saw it.
  { kind: 'punctuation', pattern: /[{}[\]().,;:?!=+\-*/%&|^~]+/y },
  { kind: 'punctuation', pattern: /[<>]/y }
];

const SHELL_RULES: Rule[] = [
  { kind: 'comment', pattern: /#[^\n]*/y, where: afterSpace },
  { kind: 'literal', pattern: /'[^'\n]*'|"(?:[^"\\\n]|\\.)*"/y },
  { kind: 'name', pattern: /\$\{[^}\n]*\}|\$[A-Za-z_]\w*/y },
  {
    kind: 'keyword',
    pattern: /\b(?:case|do|done|elif|else|esac|export|fi|for|function|if|in|local|return|sudo|then|while)\b/y
  },
  { kind: 'keyword', pattern: /--?[A-Za-z][\w-]*/y, where: afterSpace },
  // The first word of a line is the program being run. Subcommands and paths after
  // it stay plain, which keeps a long command from turning into confetti.
  { kind: 'name', pattern: /[A-Za-z_][\w./-]*/y, where: ({ atLineStart }) => atLineStart },
  { kind: 'literal', pattern: /\d[\w.]*/y, where: notInWord },
  { kind: 'punctuation', pattern: /[|&;<>()]+/y }
];

const JSON_RULES: Rule[] = [
  { kind: 'name', pattern: /"(?:[^"\\\n]|\\.)*"(?=\s*:)/y },
  { kind: 'literal', pattern: /"(?:[^"\\\n]|\\.)*"/y },
  { kind: 'keyword', pattern: /\b(?:true|false|null)\b/y },
  { kind: 'literal', pattern: /-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?/y, where: notInWord },
  { kind: 'punctuation', pattern: /[{}[\],:]+/y }
];

const CSS_RULES: Rule[] = [
  { kind: 'comment', pattern: /\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//y },
  { kind: 'keyword', pattern: /@[\w-]+/y },
  { kind: 'name', pattern: /--[\w-]+/y },
  { kind: 'literal', pattern: /'[^'\n]*'|"[^"\n]*"/y },
  { kind: 'literal', pattern: /#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}\b/y },
  { kind: 'name', pattern: /[a-zA-Z-][\w-]*(?=\s*:)/y, where: notInWord },
  { kind: 'name', pattern: /[\w-]+(?=\()/y, where: notInWord },
  { kind: 'literal', pattern: /-?(?:\d+\.?\d*|\.\d+)(?:[a-z%]+)?/y, where: notInWord },
  { kind: 'punctuation', pattern: /[{}()[\];:,.>+~*]+/y }
];

const HTML_RULES: Rule[] = [
  { kind: 'comment', pattern: /<!--[\s\S]*?-->/y },
  { kind: 'keyword', pattern: /<!\w+/y },
  { kind: 'name', pattern: /<\/?[a-zA-Z][\w-]*/y },
  { kind: 'literal', pattern: /"[^"\n]*"|'[^'\n]*'/y },
  { kind: 'keyword', pattern: /[a-zA-Z-][\w-]*(?=\s*=)/y, where: notInWord },
  { kind: 'punctuation', pattern: /[/=]+/y },
  { kind: 'punctuation', pattern: /[<>]/y }
];

const RULES = {
  shell: SHELL_RULES,
  js: JS_RULES,
  json: JSON_RULES,
  css: CSS_RULES,
  html: HTML_RULES
} as const;

const RULESET: Record<Language, keyof typeof RULES> = {
  shell: 'shell',
  bash: 'shell',
  sh: 'shell',
  zsh: 'shell',
  console: 'shell',
  js: 'js',
  javascript: 'js',
  jsx: 'js',
  ts: 'js',
  typescript: 'js',
  tsx: 'js',
  json: 'json',
  css: 'css',
  html: 'html'
};

function atLineStart(code: string, cursor: number) {
  for (let index = cursor - 1; index >= 0; index--) {
    const char = code[index];
    if (char === '\n') return true;
    if (char !== ' ' && char !== '\t') return false;
  }
  return true;
}

/**
 * Split `code` into coloured tokens. Unmatched text comes back as `plain` runs
 * rather than being dropped, so the result always reassembles into the input.
 */
export function tokenize(code: string, language: Language): Token[] {
  const rules = RULES[RULESET[language]];
  const tokens: Token[] = [];
  let cursor = 0;
  let plainStart = -1;

  function flushPlain(end: number) {
    if (plainStart < 0) return;
    tokens.push({ kind: 'plain', value: code.slice(plainStart, end), start: plainStart });
    plainStart = -1;
  }

  while (cursor < code.length) {
    const position: Cursor = {
      previous: cursor > 0 ? code[cursor - 1] : undefined,
      atLineStart: atLineStart(code, cursor)
    };

    let match: Token | undefined;
    for (const rule of rules) {
      if (rule.where && !rule.where(position)) continue;
      rule.pattern.lastIndex = cursor;
      const found = rule.pattern.exec(code);
      // A zero-length match would never advance the cursor.
      if (found && found[0].length > 0) {
        match = { kind: rule.kind, value: found[0], start: cursor };
        break;
      }
    }

    if (!match) {
      if (plainStart < 0) plainStart = cursor;
      cursor += 1;
      continue;
    }

    flushPlain(cursor);
    tokens.push(match);
    cursor += match.value.length;
  }

  flushPlain(code.length);
  return tokens;
}
````

## Accordion (`accordion`)

Accordion built on Base UI.

- Type: `registry:ui`
- Install: `npx @ternetin/ui add accordion`
- npm dependencies: `@base-ui/react@^1.9.0`
- Registry dependencies: `utils`

### `src/ui/accordion.tsx`

````tsx
'use client';
import { Accordion as BaseAccordion } from '@base-ui/react/accordion';
import { cva, type VariantProps } from 'class-variance-authority';
import type * as React from 'react';
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils';

const accordionVariants = cva('w-full', {
  variants: {
    variant: {
      default: 'border border-border',
      ghost: 'border-none bg-transparent'
    }
  },
  defaultVariants: {
    variant: 'default'
  }
});
export interface AccordionProps
  extends React.ComponentProps<typeof BaseAccordion.Root>,
    VariantProps<typeof accordionVariants> {}
export function Accordion({ className, variant, ...props }: AccordionProps) {
  return (
    <BaseAccordion.Root
      className={cn(
        accordionVariants({ variant }),
        // The root is the element with the border, so it owns the radius. Items
        // are clipped to it — rounding an item on its own does nothing, because
        // the root's square corners still draw over it.
        'overflow-hidden',
        variant !== 'ghost' && '[&>[data-slot=accordion-item]]:!rounded-none',
        'rounded-surface',
        className
      )}
      {...props}
    />
  );
}
export function AccordionItem({ className, ...props }: React.ComponentProps<typeof BaseAccordion.Item>) {
  return (
    <BaseAccordion.Item
      data-slot="accordion-item"
      className={cn('border-b border-border last:border-b-0', 'rounded-surface', className)}
      {...props}
    />
  );
}
export function AccordionTrigger({
  className,
  children,
  ...props
}: React.ComponentProps<typeof BaseAccordion.Trigger>) {
  return (
    <BaseAccordion.Header>
      <BaseAccordion.Trigger
        className={cn(
          'flex w-full items-center justify-between gap-2 px-4 py-3 text-left text-sm font-medium tracking-[-0.01em] outline-none transition-colors',
          'hover:bg-accent hover:text-accent-foreground focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring focus-visible:ring-inset',
          '[&>svg]:transition-transform [&[data-panel-open]>svg]:rotate-180',
          className
        )}
        {...props}
      >
        {children}
        <svg
          viewBox="0 0 16 16"
          className="size-4 shrink-0"
          fill="none"
          stroke="currentColor"
          strokeWidth={2}
          aria-hidden="true"
        >
          <path d="M4 6l4 4 4-4" />
        </svg>
      </BaseAccordion.Trigger>
    </BaseAccordion.Header>
  );
}
export function AccordionPanel({ className, ...props }: React.ComponentProps<typeof BaseAccordion.Panel>) {
  return (
    <BaseAccordion.Panel
      className={cn(
        // This panel animates in CSS rather than with Motion, and it has to.
        // Base UI measures the content and publishes the target height as
        // `--accordion-panel-height`, then removes the panel from the DOM once
        // its CSS transition finishes. Motion starts its animations in an effect
        // after paint, which is too late for that check — the panel is already
        // gone, so a collapse never plays. A CSS transition is declared up front
        // and is visible to Base UI immediately, so it animates both ways.
        //
        // `overflow-hidden` makes the height change read as a reveal instead of a
        // squash: the content keeps its natural size and is clipped as it grows.
        'h-[var(--accordion-panel-height)] overflow-hidden bg-secondary text-sm text-muted-foreground',
        'transition-[height,opacity] duration-300 ease-[cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1)] motion-reduce:transition-none',
        'data-[starting-style]:h-0 data-[starting-style]:opacity-0',
        'data-[ending-style]:h-0 data-[ending-style]:opacity-0',
        '[&>*]:px-4 [&>*]:py-3',
        className
      )}
      {...props}
    />
  );
}
export { accordionVariants };
````

## Alert Dialog (`alert-dialog`)

Alert Dialog built on Base UI.

- Type: `registry:ui`
- Install: `npx @ternetin/ui add alert-dialog`
- npm dependencies: `@base-ui/react@^1.9.0`
- Registry dependencies: `utils`, `motion`

### `src/ui/alert-dialog.tsx`

````tsx
'use client';
import { AlertDialog as BaseAlertDialog } from '@base-ui/react/alert-dialog';
import type * as React from 'react';
import { useMotionBackdropRender, useMotionPopupRender } from '@/lib/motion';
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils';
export const AlertDialog = BaseAlertDialog.Root;
export const AlertDialogTrigger = BaseAlertDialog.Trigger;
export const AlertDialogClose = BaseAlertDialog.Close;
export function AlertDialogContent({
  className,
  children,
  ...props
}: React.ComponentProps<typeof BaseAlertDialog.Popup>) {
  const renderBackdrop = useMotionBackdropRender();
  // No anchor to grow from, so it scales in place rather than sliding.
  const renderPopup = useMotionPopupRender({ scale: 0.97, offset: 0 });
  return (
    <BaseAlertDialog.Portal>
      <BaseAlertDialog.Backdrop className="fixed inset-0 z-50 bg-foreground/40" render={renderBackdrop} />
      <BaseAlertDialog.Popup
        className={cn(
          'fixed left-1/2 top-1/2 z-50 grid w-[calc(100%-2rem)] max-w-md -translate-x-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 gap-4',
          'border border-border bg-background p-5 outline-none',
          'shadow-modal',
          'rounded-surface',
          className
        )}
        render={renderPopup}
        {...props}
      >
        {children}
      </BaseAlertDialog.Popup>
    </BaseAlertDialog.Portal>
  );
}
export function AlertDialogTitle({ className, ...props }: React.ComponentProps<typeof BaseAlertDialog.Title>) {
  return (
    <BaseAlertDialog.Title
      className={cn('text-lg font-semibold leading-none tracking-[-0.02em]', className)}
      {...props}
    />
  );
}
export function AlertDialogDescription({
  className,
  ...props
}: React.ComponentProps<typeof BaseAlertDialog.Description>) {
  return (
    <BaseAlertDialog.Description className={cn('text-sm leading-6 text-muted-foreground', className)} {...props} />
  );
}
export function AlertDialogFooter({ className, ...props }: React.ComponentProps<'div'>) {
  return <div className={cn('flex flex-col-reverse gap-2 sm:flex-row sm:justify-end', className)} {...props} />;
}
````

## Autocomplete (`autocomplete`)

Autocomplete built on Base UI.

- Type: `registry:ui`
- Install: `npx @ternetin/ui add autocomplete`
- npm dependencies: `@base-ui/react@^1.9.0`
- Registry dependencies: `utils`, `motion`

### `src/ui/autocomplete.tsx`

````tsx
'use client';
import { Autocomplete as BaseAutocomplete } from '@base-ui/react/autocomplete';
import type * as React from 'react';
import { useMotionPopupRender } from '@/lib/motion';
import { cn, NESTED_RADIUS } from '@/lib/utils';
export const Autocomplete = BaseAutocomplete.Root;
export function AutocompleteInput({ className, ...props }: React.ComponentProps<typeof BaseAutocomplete.Input>) {
  return (
    <BaseAutocomplete.Input
      className={cn(
        'flex h-9 w-full border border-input bg-background px-3 py-2 text-sm leading-5 outline-none focus-visible:border-ring focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring',
        'rounded-control',
        className
      )}
      {...props}
    />
  );
}
export function AutocompleteContent({
  className,
  children,
  sideOffset = 4,
  style,
  ...props
}: React.ComponentProps<typeof BaseAutocomplete.Popup> & {
  sideOffset?: number;
}) {
  // Matches Combobox: slide and fade, no scale on a live results list.
  const renderPopup = useMotionPopupRender({ scale: 1, offset: 6 });
  return (
    <BaseAutocomplete.Portal>
      <BaseAutocomplete.Positioner sideOffset={sideOffset} className="z-50">
        <BaseAutocomplete.Popup
          // Nested items follow the fixed popup corner treatment.
          style={style}
          className={cn(
            'max-h-64 min-w-[var(--anchor-width)] overflow-y-auto border border-border bg-popover p-1 text-popover-foreground outline-none',
            'shadow-popup',
            'rounded-surface',
            className
          )}
          render={renderPopup}
          {...props}
        >
          <BaseAutocomplete.Empty className="px-3 py-2 text-sm leading-5 text-muted-foreground empty:p-0">
            No results.
          </BaseAutocomplete.Empty>
          <BaseAutocomplete.List>{children}</BaseAutocomplete.List>
        </BaseAutocomplete.Popup>
      </BaseAutocomplete.Positioner>
    </BaseAutocomplete.Portal>
  );
}
export function AutocompleteItem({ className, ...props }: React.ComponentProps<typeof BaseAutocomplete.Item>) {
  return (
    <BaseAutocomplete.Item
      className={cn(
        'flex cursor-pointer select-none items-center gap-2 px-3 py-1.5 text-sm leading-5 outline-none data-[highlighted]:bg-accent data-[highlighted]:text-accent-foreground',
        NESTED_RADIUS,
        className
      )}
      {...props}
    />
  );
}
````

## Card (`card`)

Composable flat card with semantic variants, shared geometry, and optional public-page corner brackets.

- Type: `registry:ui`
- Install: `npx @ternetin/ui add card`
- npm dependencies: `class-variance-authority@^0.7.1`
- Registry dependencies: `utils`

### `src/ui/card.tsx`

````tsx
'use client';
import { cva, type VariantProps } from 'class-variance-authority';
import type * as React from 'react';
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils';

const cardVariants = cva('flex flex-col gap-4 text-card-foreground', {
  variants: {
    variant: {
      default: 'border border-border bg-card',
      outline: 'border border-border bg-transparent',
      muted: 'border border-transparent bg-secondary',
      ghost: 'border border-transparent bg-transparent'
    },
    padding: {
      none: 'p-0',
      sm: 'p-3',
      md: 'p-5',
      lg: 'p-6'
    },
    corners: {
      none: '',
      diagonal: 'relative',
      all: 'relative'
    }
  },
  defaultVariants: {
    variant: 'default',
    padding: 'md',
    corners: 'none'
  }
});
/**
 * Decorative corner brackets — L-shaped arms tracing a corner of the card.
 *
 * Each bracket sits 1px outside the card so its arm covers the border it traces.
 * Use brackets on selected public pages, keeping operational cards undecorated.
 *
 * Tunable per instance through CSS variables, so a card can restyle its brackets
 * without reaching into these classes:
 *   --card-corner-size    arm length             (default 1.125rem)
 *   --card-corner-width   arm thickness          (default 3px)
 *   --card-corner-color   trailing bracket color (default foreground)
 *   --card-corner-accent  leading bracket color  (default primary)
 */
const CORNER_BASE = 'pointer-events-none absolute size-[var(--card-corner-size,1.125rem)]';
const CORNER_ARMS = {
  'top-left':
    '-top-px -left-px border-t-[length:var(--card-corner-width,3px)] border-l-[length:var(--card-corner-width,3px)]',
  'top-right':
    '-top-px -right-px border-t-[length:var(--card-corner-width,3px)] border-r-[length:var(--card-corner-width,3px)]',
  'bottom-left':
    '-bottom-px -left-px border-b-[length:var(--card-corner-width,3px)] border-l-[length:var(--card-corner-width,3px)]',
  'bottom-right':
    '-bottom-px -right-px border-b-[length:var(--card-corner-width,3px)] border-r-[length:var(--card-corner-width,3px)]'
} as const;
type Corner = keyof typeof CORNER_ARMS;
/** Which brackets each `corners` value draws. */
const CORNER_LAYOUT: Record<'none' | 'diagonal' | 'all', readonly Corner[]> = {
  none: [],
  diagonal: ['top-left', 'bottom-right'],
  all: ['top-left', 'top-right', 'bottom-left', 'bottom-right']
};
const ACCENT_TINT = 'border-[color:var(--card-corner-accent,var(--color-primary))]';
const PLAIN_TINT = 'border-[color:var(--card-corner-color,var(--color-foreground))]';
/** `split` accents the leading (top-left) bracket only; the rest stay foreground. */
function cornerTint(corner: Corner, tone: CornerTone) {
  if (tone === 'primary') return ACCENT_TINT;
  if (tone === 'foreground') return PLAIN_TINT;
  return corner === 'top-left' ? ACCENT_TINT : PLAIN_TINT;
}
export type CornerTone = 'split' | 'primary' | 'foreground';
export interface CardProps extends React.ComponentProps<'div'>, VariantProps<typeof cardVariants> {
  /** Colour of the brackets drawn by `corners`. Ignored when `corners="none"`. */
  cornerTone?: CornerTone;
}
export function Card({ className, variant, padding, corners, cornerTone = 'split', children, ...props }: CardProps) {
  const placement = corners ?? 'none';
  return (
    <div
      className={cn(cardVariants({ variant, padding, corners: placement }), 'rounded-surface', className)}
      {...props}
    >
      {CORNER_LAYOUT[placement].map((corner) => (
        <span
          key={corner}
          aria-hidden="true"
          className={cn(CORNER_BASE, CORNER_ARMS[corner], cornerTint(corner, cornerTone))}
        />
      ))}
      {children}
    </div>
  );
}
export function CardHeader({ className, ...props }: React.ComponentProps<'div'>) {
  return <div className={cn('flex flex-col gap-1', className)} {...props} />;
}
export function CardTitle({ className, ...props }: React.ComponentProps<'div'>) {
  return <div className={cn('text-lg font-semibold leading-none tracking-[-0.02em]', className)} {...props} />;
}
export function CardDescription({ className, ...props }: React.ComponentProps<'div'>) {
  return <div className={cn('text-sm text-muted-foreground', className)} {...props} />;
}
export function CardContent({ className, ...props }: React.ComponentProps<'div'>) {
  return <div className={cn('text-sm', className)} {...props} />;
}
export function CardFooter({ className, ...props }: React.ComponentProps<'div'>) {
  return <div className={cn('flex items-center gap-2', className)} {...props} />;
}
export { cardVariants };
````

## Checkbox (`checkbox`)

Checkbox built on Base UI.

- Type: `registry:ui`
- Install: `npx @ternetin/ui add checkbox`
- npm dependencies: `@base-ui/react@^1.9.0`, `motion@^12.43.0`
- Registry dependencies: `utils`, `motion`

### `src/ui/checkbox.tsx`

````tsx
'use client';
import { Checkbox as BaseCheckbox } from '@base-ui/react/checkbox';
import { type HTMLMotionProps, motion } from 'motion/react';
import type * as React from 'react';
import { transitions, useControlTransition } from '@/lib/motion';
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils';
export function Checkbox({ className, ...props }: React.ComponentProps<typeof BaseCheckbox.Root>) {
  const transition = useControlTransition();
  return (
    <BaseCheckbox.Root
      className={cn(
        'flex size-5 shrink-0 items-center justify-center border border-input bg-background outline-none transition-colors',
        'focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring',
        'data-[checked]:border-primary data-[checked]:bg-primary data-[checked]:text-primary-foreground',
        'disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:opacity-40',
        'rounded-control',
        className
      )}
      {...props}
    >
      {/*
          `keepMounted` so the tick can animate both ways. Without it Base UI drops
          the indicator from the DOM the moment the box is unticked, and there's
          nothing left to animate out.
        */}
      <BaseCheckbox.Indicator
        keepMounted
        className="flex text-current"
        render={(indicatorProps, state) => (
          <motion.span
            {...(indicatorProps as HTMLMotionProps<'span'>)}
            initial={false}
            animate={{ opacity: state.checked ? 1 : 0, scale: state.checked ? 1 : 0.6 }}
            transition={transition}
          >
            <svg
              viewBox="0 0 16 16"
              className="size-3.5"
              fill="none"
              stroke="currentColor"
              strokeWidth={3}
              aria-hidden="true"
            >
              {/* The tick draws itself on rather than just fading in. */}
              <motion.path
                d="M3 8l3.5 3.5L13 4"
                strokeLinecap="square"
                initial={false}
                animate={{ pathLength: state.checked ? 1 : 0 }}
                transition={state.checked ? transitions.enter : transitions.exit}
              />
            </svg>
          </motion.span>
        )}
      />
    </BaseCheckbox.Root>
  );
}
````

## Code (`code`)

Single-line or multi-line code snippet with an optional title strip, syntax highlighting and a copy button. Plain styled container — not a Base UI primitive.

- Type: `registry:ui`
- Install: `npx @ternetin/ui add code`
- npm dependencies: `@base-ui/react@^1.9.0`, `motion@^12.43.0`, `class-variance-authority@^0.7.1`
- Registry dependencies: `utils`, `motion`, `highlight`

### `src/ui/code.tsx`

````tsx
'use client';
import { Button as BaseButton } from '@base-ui/react/button';
import { cva, type VariantProps } from 'class-variance-authority';
import { type HTMLMotionProps, motion } from 'motion/react';
import * as React from 'react';
import { type Language, type TokenKind, tokenize } from '@/lib/highlight';
import { useTapMotion } from '@/lib/motion';
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils';

const codeVariants = cva('flex w-full min-w-0 flex-col overflow-hidden font-mono font-medium', {
  variants: {
    variant: {
      default: 'border-l-[3px] border-l-primary bg-primary/[0.06] text-foreground',
      outline: 'border border-border border-l-[3px] border-l-primary bg-background text-primary',
      muted: 'border-l-[3px] border-l-border bg-muted text-foreground',
      ghost: 'border-l-[3px] border-l-transparent bg-transparent text-foreground'
    },
    size: {
      sm: 'text-xs',
      default: 'text-sm',
      lg: 'text-base'
    }
  },
  defaultVariants: {
    variant: 'default',
    size: 'default'
  }
});
/**
 * How each size packs its rows. Separate from the cva above, which only sets the
 * type scale and the box's colours — these are the metrics the header, the snippet
 * row and the copy button have to agree on.
 *
 *  header  the title strip, deliberately tighter than the snippet row
 *  row     the snippet row
 *  inset   tightens whichever row holds the copy button, since the button carries
 *          its own optical padding around the icon
 *  button  the button box; the negative margin lets a button taller than the line
 *          it sits on bleed into the row's padding instead of growing the row
 *  label   the title's own type scale — meta text, a step down from the code
 */
const SIZES = {
  sm: {
    header: 'px-2.5 py-1',
    row: 'gap-1.5 px-2.5 py-1.5',
    inset: 'pr-1',
    button: '-my-1 size-6 [&_svg]:size-3.5',
    label: 'text-xs'
  },
  default: {
    header: 'px-3 py-1.5',
    row: 'gap-2 px-3 py-2',
    inset: 'pr-1.5',
    button: '-my-1 size-7 [&_svg]:size-4',
    label: 'text-xs'
  },
  lg: {
    header: 'px-4 py-2',
    row: 'gap-2.5 px-4 py-3',
    inset: 'pr-2',
    button: '-my-1 size-8 [&_svg]:size-4.5',
    label: 'text-sm'
  }
} as const;
/**
 * `whitespace-pre` is the whole difference between the two modes: a block keeps
 * its line breaks, and a one-liner is forbidden from wrapping — it scrolls
 * sideways instead, so the row keeps its height and the copy button never moves.
 */
const CONTENT = 'min-w-0 flex-1 overflow-x-auto whitespace-pre';
const HEADER = 'flex items-center justify-between gap-2 border-b border-border font-semibold tracking-[-0.01em]';
/**
 * Token colours. Three inks and no more, defined in the theme: the house blue for
 * language keywords, a violet for names, a green for literals. Comments and
 * punctuation recede into grey, and anything unclassified stays ink.
 */
const TOKEN_CLASS: Record<TokenKind, string> = {
  plain: '',
  comment: 'font-normal text-muted-foreground',
  keyword: 'text-syntax-keyword',
  literal: 'text-syntax-literal',
  name: 'text-syntax-name',
  punctuation: 'text-muted-foreground'
};
/**
 * The confirmed state borrows --syntax-keyword rather than --primary: it's the
 * same house blue in light mode, but lifted in dark, where #0047ff as a 16px icon
 * on black sits at about 2.3:1.
 */
const COPY_BUTTON =
  'inline-flex shrink-0 cursor-pointer items-center justify-center border border-transparent text-current transition-colors outline-none hover:bg-foreground/10 focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring focus-visible:ring-inset disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:opacity-40 data-[copied]:text-syntax-keyword [&_svg]:shrink-0';
function CopyIcon() {
  return (
    <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" strokeWidth={2} aria-hidden="true">
      <path d="M11.5 6V2.5H2.5v9H6" />
      <rect x="6" y="6" width="7.5" height="7.5" />
    </svg>
  );
}
function CheckIcon() {
  return (
    <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" strokeWidth={2} aria-hidden="true">
      <path d="M3 8.5 6.5 12 13 4.5" />
    </svg>
  );
}
export interface CodeCopyButtonProps extends Omit<React.ComponentProps<typeof BaseButton>, 'children'> {
  /** Text to copy. Falls back to the text content of `target`. */
  code?: string;
  /** Element whose text content is copied when `code` isn't given. */
  target?: React.RefObject<HTMLElement | null>;
  /** Called with the text that reached the clipboard. Not called on a failed write. */
  onCopied?: (code: string) => void;
  /**
   * Accessible name.
   * @default 'Copy code'
   */
  label?: string;
  /**
   * Accessible name and announcement once the text is on the clipboard.
   * @default 'Copied'
   */
  copiedLabel?: string;
  /**
   * How long the confirmation state stays on screen, in ms.
   * @default 2000
   */
  copiedDuration?: number;
}
/**
 * Copy-to-clipboard button. Rendered inside {@link Code} by default; export is
 * for placing one somewhere else — a card header, a table row — against a
 * `target` element or an explicit `code` string.
 */
export function CodeCopyButton({
  className,
  code,
  target,
  onCopied,
  label = 'Copy code',
  copiedLabel = 'Copied',
  copiedDuration = 2000,
  onClick,
  ...props
}: CodeCopyButtonProps) {
  const [copied, setCopied] = React.useState(false);
  const tap = useTapMotion();
  React.useEffect(() => {
    if (!copied) return;
    const timer = window.setTimeout(() => setCopied(false), copiedDuration);
    return () => window.clearTimeout(timer);
  }, [copied, copiedDuration]);
  async function writeToClipboard() {
    const text = code ?? target?.current?.textContent ?? '';
    if (!text) return;
    try {
      await navigator.clipboard.writeText(text);
    } catch {
      // Clipboard writes are refused outside a secure context, and under some
      // permission policies. Leave the button alone rather than confirm a copy
      // that never landed.
      return;
    }
    setCopied(true);
    onCopied?.(text);
  }
  return (
    <BaseButton
      aria-label={copied ? copiedLabel : label}
      data-copied={copied || undefined}
      className={cn(COPY_BUTTON, className)}
      onClick={(event) => {
        onClick?.(event);
        void writeToClipboard();
      }}
      render={(buttonProps) => <motion.button {...(buttonProps as HTMLMotionProps<'button'>)} {...tap} />}
      {...props}
    >
      {copied ? <CheckIcon /> : <CopyIcon />}
      {/* A swapped aria-label isn't announced on a button that already has focus. */}
      <span aria-live="polite" className="sr-only">
        {copied ? copiedLabel : ''}
      </span>
    </BaseButton>
  );
}
export interface CodeProps extends React.ComponentProps<'div'>, VariantProps<typeof codeVariants> {
  /**
   * Text handed to the clipboard. Defaults to the rendered text content, so it
   * only needs setting when the children aren't the literal snippet — a
   * highlighted or truncated rendering, say.
   */
  code?: string;
  /**
   * Filename or label for the snippet, shown in a strip above it. The copy button
   * moves up into that strip, off the code itself.
   */
  title?: string;
  /**
   * Colour the snippet's syntax. Only applies to plain-string children: there's
   * nothing to tokenize in an already-rendered tree, so pass a string and let this
   * do the highlighting, or pass your own spans and leave it off.
   */
  language?: Language;
  /**
   * Render as a block that keeps its line breaks. Inferred from the snippet when
   * left unset: anything with a newline in it becomes a block, a one-liner stays
   * a single row. Set it explicitly when the children aren't a plain string.
   */
  multiline?: boolean;
  /**
   * Show the copy button.
   * @default true
   */
  copy?: boolean;
  /** Called with the text that reached the clipboard. */
  onCopied?: (code: string) => void;
}
/**
 * A command, token or snippet, with a copy button and optional syntax colouring.
 * Plain styled container — not a Base UI primitive.
 */
export function Code({
  className,
  variant,
  size,
  code,
  title,
  language,
  multiline,
  copy = true,
  onCopied,
  children,
  ...props
}: CodeProps) {
  const contentRef = React.useRef<HTMLElement | null>(null);
  const setContentRef = (element: HTMLElement | null) => {
    contentRef.current = element;
  };
  const source = typeof children === 'string' ? children : undefined;
  const block = multiline ?? (code ?? source)?.includes('\n') ?? false;
  const metrics = SIZES[size ?? 'default'];
  const tokens = React.useMemo(
    () => (language && source !== undefined ? tokenize(source, language) : undefined),
    [language, source]
  );
  // Plain runs stay bare strings: fewer elements, and the copy button reads the
  // same text content either way.
  const content = tokens
    ? tokens.map((token) =>
        token.kind === 'plain' ? (
          token.value
        ) : (
          <span key={token.start} className={TOKEN_CLASS[token.kind]}>
            {token.value}
          </span>
        )
      )
    : children;
  const copyButton = copy ? (
    <CodeCopyButton
      code={code}
      target={contentRef}
      onCopied={onCopied}
      label={title ? `Copy ${title}` : undefined}
      className={metrics.button}
    />
  ) : null;
  return (
    <div
      data-multiline={block || undefined}
      className={cn(codeVariants({ variant, size }), 'rounded-surface', className)}
      {...props}
    >
      {title ? (
        <div className={cn(HEADER, metrics.header, copy && metrics.inset)}>
          <span className={cn('truncate text-foreground', metrics.label)}>{title}</span>
          {copyButton}
        </div>
      ) : null}
      <div
        className={cn(
          'flex min-w-0',
          // A one-liner centres its copy button against the single row of text; a
          // block pins it to the first line so it stays put as the snippet grows.
          block ? 'items-start' : 'items-center',
          metrics.row,
          !title && copy && metrics.inset
        )}
      >
        {block ? (
          <pre ref={setContentRef} className={CONTENT}>
            <code>{content}</code>
          </pre>
        ) : (
          <code ref={setContentRef} className={CONTENT}>
            {content}
          </code>
        )}
        {title ? null : copyButton}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
/** Stacked snippets — a run of one-liners read as a sequence to type in order. */
export function CodeStack({ className, ...props }: React.ComponentProps<'div'>) {
  return <div className={cn('grid w-full gap-2', className)} {...props} />;
}
export { codeVariants };
````

## Collapsible (`collapsible`)

Collapsible built on Base UI.

- Type: `registry:ui`
- Install: `npx @ternetin/ui add collapsible`
- npm dependencies: `@base-ui/react@^1.9.0`
- Registry dependencies: `utils`

### `src/ui/collapsible.tsx`

````tsx
'use client';
import { Collapsible as BaseCollapsible } from '@base-ui/react/collapsible';
import { cva, type VariantProps } from 'class-variance-authority';
import type * as React from 'react';
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils';

const collapsibleVariants = cva('', {
  variants: {
    variant: {
      default: 'border border-border',
      ghost: 'border-none bg-transparent'
    }
  },
  defaultVariants: {
    variant: 'default'
  }
});
export interface CollapsibleProps
  extends React.ComponentProps<typeof BaseCollapsible.Root>,
    VariantProps<typeof collapsibleVariants> {}
export function Collapsible({ className, variant, ...props }: CollapsibleProps) {
  return <BaseCollapsible.Root className={cn(collapsibleVariants({ variant }), className)} {...props} />;
}
export function CollapsibleTrigger({
  className,
  children,
  ...props
}: React.ComponentProps<typeof BaseCollapsible.Trigger>) {
  return (
    <BaseCollapsible.Trigger
      className={cn(
        'flex items-center justify-between gap-2 text-sm font-medium tracking-[-0.01em] outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring',
        '[&>svg]:transition-transform [&[data-panel-open]>svg]:rotate-180',
        className
      )}
      {...props}
    >
      {children}
      <svg
        viewBox="0 0 16 16"
        className="size-4 shrink-0"
        fill="none"
        stroke="currentColor"
        strokeWidth={2}
        aria-hidden="true"
      >
        <path d="M4 6l4 4 4-4" />
      </svg>
    </BaseCollapsible.Trigger>
  );
}
export function CollapsiblePanel({ className, ...props }: React.ComponentProps<typeof BaseCollapsible.Panel>) {
  return (
    <BaseCollapsible.Panel
      className={cn(
        // CSS rather than Motion, for the reason spelled out in accordion.tsx:
        // Base UI unmounts this panel when its CSS transition ends, and Motion's
        // animations start too late to be seen by that check.
        'h-[var(--collapsible-panel-height)] overflow-hidden bg-secondary text-sm text-muted-foreground',
        'transition-[height,opacity] duration-300 ease-[cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1)] motion-reduce:transition-none',
        'data-[starting-style]:h-0 data-[starting-style]:opacity-0',
        'data-[ending-style]:h-0 data-[ending-style]:opacity-0',
        'rounded-surface',
        className
      )}
      {...props}
    />
  );
}
export { collapsibleVariants };
````

## Combobox (`combobox`)

Combobox built on Base UI.

- Type: `registry:ui`
- Install: `npx @ternetin/ui add combobox`
- npm dependencies: `@base-ui/react@^1.9.0`
- Registry dependencies: `utils`, `motion`

### `src/ui/combobox.tsx`

````tsx
'use client';
import { Combobox as BaseCombobox } from '@base-ui/react/combobox';
import type * as React from 'react';
import { useMotionPopupRender } from '@/lib/motion';
import { cn, NESTED_RADIUS } from '@/lib/utils';
export const Combobox = BaseCombobox.Root;
export const ComboboxValue = BaseCombobox.Value;
export function ComboboxInput({ className, ...props }: React.ComponentProps<typeof BaseCombobox.Input>) {
  return (
    <BaseCombobox.Input
      className={cn(
        'flex h-9 w-full border border-input bg-background px-3 py-2 text-sm leading-5 outline-none focus-visible:border-ring focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring',
        'rounded-control',
        className
      )}
      {...props}
    />
  );
}
export function ComboboxContent({
  className,
  children,
  sideOffset = 4,
  style,
  ...props
}: React.ComponentProps<typeof BaseCombobox.Popup> & {
  sideOffset?: number;
}) {
  // A results list appearing under an input: no scale, it would look like a
  // zoom on text the user is actively reading. Just a short slide and fade.
  const renderPopup = useMotionPopupRender({ scale: 1, offset: 6 });
  return (
    <BaseCombobox.Portal>
      <BaseCombobox.Positioner sideOffset={sideOffset} className="z-50">
        <BaseCombobox.Popup
          // Nested items follow the fixed popup corner treatment.
          style={style}
          className={cn(
            'max-h-64 min-w-[var(--anchor-width)] overflow-y-auto border border-border bg-popover p-1 text-popover-foreground shadow-popup outline-none',
            'rounded-surface',
            className
          )}
          render={renderPopup}
          {...props}
        >
          <BaseCombobox.Empty className="px-3 py-2 text-sm leading-5 text-muted-foreground empty:p-0">
            No results.
          </BaseCombobox.Empty>
          <BaseCombobox.List>{children}</BaseCombobox.List>
        </BaseCombobox.Popup>
      </BaseCombobox.Positioner>
    </BaseCombobox.Portal>
  );
}
export function ComboboxItem({ className, children, ...props }: React.ComponentProps<typeof BaseCombobox.Item>) {
  return (
    <BaseCombobox.Item
      className={cn(
        'flex cursor-pointer select-none items-center justify-between gap-2 px-3 py-1.5 text-sm leading-5 outline-none data-[highlighted]:bg-accent data-[highlighted]:text-accent-foreground',
        NESTED_RADIUS,
        className
      )}
      {...props}
    >
      {children}
      <BaseCombobox.ItemIndicator>✓</BaseCombobox.ItemIndicator>
    </BaseCombobox.Item>
  );
}
````

## Context Menu (`context-menu`)

Context Menu built on Base UI.

- Type: `registry:ui`
- Install: `npx @ternetin/ui add context-menu`
- npm dependencies: `@base-ui/react@^1.9.0`
- Registry dependencies: `utils`, `motion`

### `src/ui/context-menu.tsx`

````tsx
'use client';
import { ContextMenu as BaseContextMenu } from '@base-ui/react/context-menu';
import type * as React from 'react';
import { useMotionPopupRender } from '@/lib/motion';
import { cn, NESTED_RADIUS } from '@/lib/utils';
export const ContextMenu = BaseContextMenu.Root;
export const ContextMenuTrigger = BaseContextMenu.Trigger;
export const ContextMenuGroup = BaseContextMenu.Group;
export function ContextMenuContent({
  className,
  children,
  style,
  ...props
}: React.ComponentProps<typeof BaseContextMenu.Popup>) {
  // Anchored to the pointer, so it grows from the click point with no slide.
  const renderPopup = useMotionPopupRender({ scale: 0.95, offset: 0 });
  return (
    <BaseContextMenu.Portal>
      <BaseContextMenu.Positioner className="z-50 outline-none">
        <BaseContextMenu.Popup
          style={style}
          className={cn(
            'min-w-40 border border-border bg-popover p-1 text-popover-foreground shadow-popup outline-none',
            '[transform-origin:var(--transform-origin)]',
            'rounded-surface',
            className
          )}
          render={renderPopup}
          {...props}
        >
          {children}
        </BaseContextMenu.Popup>
      </BaseContextMenu.Positioner>
    </BaseContextMenu.Portal>
  );
}
export function ContextMenuItem({ className, ...props }: React.ComponentProps<typeof BaseContextMenu.Item>) {
  return (
    <BaseContextMenu.Item
      className={cn(
        'flex cursor-pointer select-none items-center gap-2 px-3 py-1.5 text-sm leading-5 outline-none',
        NESTED_RADIUS,
        'data-[highlighted]:bg-accent data-[highlighted]:text-accent-foreground',
        'data-[disabled]:pointer-events-none data-[disabled]:opacity-40',
        className
      )}
      {...props}
    />
  );
}
export function ContextMenuSeparator({ className, ...props }: React.ComponentProps<'div'>) {
  return <div className={cn('-mx-1 my-1 h-px bg-border', className)} {...props} />;
}
````

## Dialog (`dialog`)

Dialog built on Base UI.

- Type: `registry:ui`
- Install: `npx @ternetin/ui add dialog`
- npm dependencies: `@base-ui/react@^1.9.0`
- Registry dependencies: `utils`, `motion`

### `src/ui/dialog.tsx`

````tsx
'use client';
import { Dialog as BaseDialog } from '@base-ui/react/dialog';
import type * as React from 'react';
import { useMotionBackdropRender, useMotionPopupRender } from '@/lib/motion';
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils';
export const Dialog = BaseDialog.Root;
export const DialogTrigger = BaseDialog.Trigger;
export const DialogClose = BaseDialog.Close;
export const DialogPortal = BaseDialog.Portal;
export function DialogContent({ className, children, ...props }: React.ComponentProps<typeof BaseDialog.Popup>) {
  const renderBackdrop = useMotionBackdropRender();
  // A dialog has no anchor to grow from, so it scales in place rather than sliding.
  const renderPopup = useMotionPopupRender({ scale: 0.97, offset: 0 });
  return (
    <BaseDialog.Portal>
      <BaseDialog.Backdrop className="fixed inset-0 z-50 bg-foreground/40" render={renderBackdrop} />
      <BaseDialog.Popup
        className={cn(
          // Tailwind centres with the standalone `translate` property, which
          // composes with the `transform` Motion writes — they don't collide.
          'fixed left-1/2 top-1/2 z-50 grid w-[calc(100%-2rem)] max-w-md -translate-x-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 gap-4',
          'border border-border bg-background p-5 outline-none',
          'shadow-modal',
          'rounded-surface',
          className
        )}
        render={renderPopup}
        {...props}
      >
        {children}
      </BaseDialog.Popup>
    </BaseDialog.Portal>
  );
}
export function DialogHeader({ className, ...props }: React.ComponentProps<'div'>) {
  return <div className={cn('flex flex-col gap-1', className)} {...props} />;
}
export function DialogFooter({ className, ...props }: React.ComponentProps<'div'>) {
  return <div className={cn('flex flex-col-reverse gap-2 sm:flex-row sm:justify-end', className)} {...props} />;
}
export function DialogTitle({ className, ...props }: React.ComponentProps<typeof BaseDialog.Title>) {
  return (
    <BaseDialog.Title className={cn('text-lg font-semibold leading-none tracking-[-0.02em]', className)} {...props} />
  );
}
export function DialogDescription({ className, ...props }: React.ComponentProps<typeof BaseDialog.Description>) {
  return <BaseDialog.Description className={cn('text-sm leading-6 text-muted-foreground', className)} {...props} />;
}
````

## Data Table (`data-table`)

Generic TanStack table with sorting, global filtering, pagination, page-size controls, and row selection.

- Type: `registry:ui`
- Install: `npx @ternetin/ui add data-table`
- npm dependencies: `@tanstack/react-table@^8.21.3`
- Registry dependencies: `utils`, `button`, `checkbox`, `input`, `select`

### `src/ui/data-table.tsx`

````tsx
'use client';
import {
  type ColumnDef,
  flexRender,
  getCoreRowModel,
  getFilteredRowModel,
  getPaginationRowModel,
  getSortedRowModel,
  type OnChangeFn,
  type RowSelectionState,
  type SortingState,
  type TableOptions,
  useReactTable
} from '@tanstack/react-table';
import { useState } from 'react';
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils';
import { Button } from '@/ui/button';
import { Checkbox } from '@/ui/checkbox';
import { Input } from '@/ui/input';
import { Select, SelectContent, SelectItem, SelectTrigger, SelectValue } from '@/ui/select';
export interface DataTableProps<TData> {
  columns: ColumnDef<TData>[];
  data: TData[];
  className?: string;
  searchPlaceholder?: string;
  emptyMessage?: string;
  initialPageSize?: number;
  pageSizeOptions?: number[];
  enableRowSelection?: boolean;
  getRowId?: TableOptions<TData>['getRowId'];
  onRowSelectionChange?: OnChangeFn<RowSelectionState>;
}
export function DataTable<TData>({
  columns,
  data,
  className,
  searchPlaceholder = 'Search...',
  emptyMessage = 'No results.',
  initialPageSize = 10,
  pageSizeOptions = [10, 20, 50],
  enableRowSelection = true,
  getRowId,
  onRowSelectionChange
}: DataTableProps<TData>) {
  const [sorting, setSorting] = useState<SortingState>([]);
  const [globalFilter, setGlobalFilter] = useState('');
  const [rowSelection, setRowSelection] = useState<RowSelectionState>({});
  const selectionColumn: ColumnDef<TData> = {
    id: 'select',
    enableHiding: false,
    enableSorting: false,
    header: ({ table }) => (
      <Checkbox
        aria-label="Select all rows on page"
        checked={table.getIsAllPageRowsSelected()}
        indeterminate={table.getIsSomePageRowsSelected()}
        onCheckedChange={(checked) => table.toggleAllPageRowsSelected(Boolean(checked))}
      />
    ),
    cell: ({ row }) => (
      <Checkbox
        aria-label="Select row"
        checked={row.getIsSelected()}
        disabled={!row.getCanSelect()}
        onCheckedChange={(checked) => row.toggleSelected(Boolean(checked))}
      />
    )
  };
  const table = useReactTable({
    data,
    columns: enableRowSelection ? [selectionColumn, ...columns] : columns,
    state: { sorting, globalFilter, rowSelection },
    initialState: { pagination: { pageSize: initialPageSize } },
    enableRowSelection,
    getRowId,
    onSortingChange: setSorting,
    onGlobalFilterChange: setGlobalFilter,
    onRowSelectionChange: (updater) => {
      setRowSelection(updater);
      onRowSelectionChange?.(updater);
    },
    getCoreRowModel: getCoreRowModel(),
    getFilteredRowModel: getFilteredRowModel(),
    getSortedRowModel: getSortedRowModel(),
    getPaginationRowModel: getPaginationRowModel()
  });
  return (
    <div className={cn('space-y-3', className)}>
      <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center justify-between gap-3">
        <Input
          type="search"
          value={globalFilter}
          onChange={(event) => setGlobalFilter(event.target.value)}
          placeholder={searchPlaceholder}
          aria-label={searchPlaceholder}
          className="max-w-sm"
        />
        <div className="flex items-center gap-2 text-sm leading-5 text-muted-foreground">
          <span>Rows per page</span>
          <Select
            value={String(table.getState().pagination.pageSize)}
            onValueChange={(value) => table.setPageSize(Number(value))}
          >
            <SelectTrigger className="h-8 w-20" aria-label="Rows per page">
              <SelectValue />
            </SelectTrigger>
            <SelectContent>
              {pageSizeOptions.map((size) => (
                <SelectItem key={size} value={String(size)}>
                  {size}
                </SelectItem>
              ))}
            </SelectContent>
          </Select>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div className={cn('overflow-x-auto border border-border bg-background', 'rounded-surface')}>
        <table className="w-full border-collapse text-sm leading-5">
          <thead className="bg-secondary text-left">
            {table.getHeaderGroups().map((headerGroup) => (
              <tr key={headerGroup.id} className="border-b border-border">
                {headerGroup.headers.map((header) => (
                  <th
                    key={header.id}
                    aria-sort={
                      header.column.getCanSort()
                        ? header.column.getIsSorted() === 'asc'
                          ? 'ascending'
                          : header.column.getIsSorted() === 'desc'
                            ? 'descending'
                            : 'none'
                        : undefined
                    }
                    className="h-11 whitespace-nowrap px-3 text-xs font-medium text-muted-foreground"
                  >
                    {header.isPlaceholder ? null : header.column.getCanSort() ? (
                      <button
                        type="button"
                        className="inline-flex items-center gap-2 outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring"
                        onClick={header.column.getToggleSortingHandler()}
                      >
                        {flexRender(header.column.columnDef.header, header.getContext())}
                        <svg
                          viewBox="0 0 16 16"
                          className="size-3.5 text-muted-foreground"
                          fill="none"
                          stroke="currentColor"
                          strokeWidth="1.5"
                          aria-hidden="true"
                        >
                          <path
                            d={
                              header.column.getIsSorted() === 'asc'
                                ? 'm4 9 4-4 4 4'
                                : header.column.getIsSorted() === 'desc'
                                  ? 'm4 6 4 4 4-4'
                                  : 'm5 6 3-3 3 3M5 10l3 3 3-3'
                            }
                          />
                        </svg>
                      </button>
                    ) : (
                      flexRender(header.column.columnDef.header, header.getContext())
                    )}
                  </th>
                ))}
              </tr>
            ))}
          </thead>
          <tbody>
            {table.getRowModel().rows.length > 0 ? (
              table.getRowModel().rows.map((row) => (
                <tr
                  key={row.id}
                  data-state={row.getIsSelected() ? 'selected' : undefined}
                  className="border-b border-border transition-colors last:border-b-0 hover:bg-accent/70 data-[state=selected]:bg-accent"
                >
                  {row.getVisibleCells().map((cell) => (
                    <td key={cell.id} className="h-12 whitespace-nowrap px-3">
                      {flexRender(cell.column.columnDef.cell, cell.getContext())}
                    </td>
                  ))}
                </tr>
              ))
            ) : (
              <tr>
                <td colSpan={table.getVisibleLeafColumns().length} className="h-24 text-center text-muted-foreground">
                  {emptyMessage}
                </td>
              </tr>
            )}
          </tbody>
        </table>
      </div>

      <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center justify-between gap-3 text-sm leading-5">
        <span className="text-muted-foreground">
          {enableRowSelection
            ? `${table.getFilteredSelectedRowModel().rows.length} of ${table.getFilteredRowModel().rows.length} selected`
            : `${table.getFilteredRowModel().rows.length} rows`}
        </span>
        <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
          <span className="mr-2 text-muted-foreground">
            Page {table.getState().pagination.pageIndex + 1} of {Math.max(table.getPageCount(), 1)}
          </span>
          <Button
            variant="outline"
            size="sm"
            aria-label="First page"
            disabled={!table.getCanPreviousPage()}
            onClick={() => table.firstPage()}
          >
            <PageChevron direction="left" double />
          </Button>
          <Button
            variant="outline"
            size="sm"
            aria-label="Previous page"
            disabled={!table.getCanPreviousPage()}
            onClick={() => table.previousPage()}
          >
            <PageChevron direction="left" />
          </Button>
          <Button
            variant="outline"
            size="sm"
            aria-label="Next page"
            disabled={!table.getCanNextPage()}
            onClick={() => table.nextPage()}
          >
            <PageChevron direction="right" />
          </Button>
          <Button
            variant="outline"
            size="sm"
            aria-label="Last page"
            disabled={!table.getCanNextPage()}
            onClick={() => table.lastPage()}
          >
            <PageChevron direction="right" double />
          </Button>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

function PageChevron({ direction, double }: { direction: 'left' | 'right'; double?: boolean }) {
  return (
    <svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" className="size-4" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" strokeWidth="1.5" aria-hidden="true">
      <path d={direction === 'left' ? 'm10 4-4 4 4 4' : 'm6 4 4 4-4 4'} />
      {double && <path d={direction === 'left' ? 'M3 3v10' : 'M13 3v10'} />}
    </svg>
  );
}
````

## Drawer (`drawer`)

Drawer built on Base UI.

- Type: `registry:ui`
- Install: `npx @ternetin/ui add drawer`
- npm dependencies: `@base-ui/react@^1.9.0`
- Registry dependencies: `utils`

### `src/ui/drawer.tsx`

````tsx
'use client';
import { Drawer as BaseDrawer } from '@base-ui/react/drawer';
import type * as React from 'react';
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils';
/**
 * Base UI dismisses a drawer along `swipeDirection`, which defaults to `'down'`.
 * This drawer is styled as a right-hand panel, so the default would have the user
 * swiping down to dismiss a sheet that slides in horizontally, and would leave the
 * backdrop's swipe-progress fade inert — Base UI only reports movement along the
 * configured axis. Override it if you restyle the drawer to enter from another edge.
 */
export function Drawer({ swipeDirection = 'right', ...props }: React.ComponentProps<typeof BaseDrawer.Root>) {
  return <BaseDrawer.Root swipeDirection={swipeDirection} {...props} />;
}
export const DrawerTrigger = BaseDrawer.Trigger;
export const DrawerClose = BaseDrawer.Close;
export function DrawerContent({ className, children, ...props }: React.ComponentProps<typeof BaseDrawer.Popup>) {
  return (
    <BaseDrawer.Portal>
      <BaseDrawer.Backdrop
        className={cn(
          'fixed inset-0 z-50 bg-foreground/40',
          // Base UI reports how far through a dismiss swipe the drawer is, as a
          // 0–1 scalar. Feeding it into opacity lets the scrim lift under the
          // finger instead of holding full strength until release.
          'opacity-[calc(1-var(--drawer-swipe-progress,0))]',
          'transition-opacity duration-200 ease-[cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1)]',
          'data-[starting-style]:opacity-0 data-[ending-style]:opacity-0',
          'data-[swiping]:transition-none'
        )}
      />
      {/*
          The viewport is required, not optional decoration: without it Base UI
          disables swipe-to-close and touch scroll locking outright, which would
          make the swipe-tracking styles below dead code.
        */}
      <BaseDrawer.Viewport className="fixed inset-y-0 right-0 z-50 flex">
        <BaseDrawer.Popup
          className={cn(
            'flex w-80 max-w-[90vw] flex-col gap-4 border-l border-border bg-background p-5 outline-none',
            // Drawer motion is CSS rather than Motion, and deliberately so: during a
            // swipe Base UI drives this element by writing `transform` directly, so
            // a `motion.div` — which owns `transform` — would stop the sheet
            // tracking the finger. See lib/motion.tsx for where Motion is used.
            //
            // Enter and exit are ours to animate, via `translate`. Base UI's drag
            // uses `transform`, and Tailwind compiles `translate-*` to the separate
            // `translate` property, so the two never overwrite each other. Don't add
            // `--drawer-swipe-movement-*` here: Base UI already applies that
            // movement itself, and reapplying it moves the drawer twice as far.
            'transition-[translate] duration-300 ease-[cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1)] motion-reduce:transition-none',
            'data-[starting-style]:[translate:100%_0] data-[ending-style]:[translate:100%_0]',
            // No easing while the finger is down — the sheet must track it 1:1.
            'data-[swiping]:transition-none',
            'rounded-surface',
            'ui-drawer-content rounded-r-none [border-bottom-right-radius:0] [border-top-right-radius:0]',
            className
          )}
          {...props}
        >
          {children}
        </BaseDrawer.Popup>
      </BaseDrawer.Viewport>
    </BaseDrawer.Portal>
  );
}
export function DrawerTitle({ className, ...props }: React.ComponentProps<typeof BaseDrawer.Title>) {
  return (
    <BaseDrawer.Title className={cn('text-lg font-semibold leading-none tracking-[-0.02em]', className)} {...props} />
  );
}
export function DrawerDescription({ className, ...props }: React.ComponentProps<typeof BaseDrawer.Description>) {
  return <BaseDrawer.Description className={cn('text-sm leading-6 text-muted-foreground', className)} {...props} />;
}
````

## Fieldset (`fieldset`)

Fieldset built on Base UI.

- Type: `registry:ui`
- Install: `npx @ternetin/ui add fieldset`
- npm dependencies: `@base-ui/react@^1.9.0`
- Registry dependencies: `utils`

### `src/ui/fieldset.tsx`

````tsx
'use client';
import { Fieldset as BaseFieldset } from '@base-ui/react/fieldset';
import { cva, type VariantProps } from 'class-variance-authority';
import type * as React from 'react';
import { cn } from '@/lib/utils';

const fieldsetVariants = cva('relative flex flex-col gap-4 p-4', {
  variants: {
    variant: {
      // `pt-6` leaves room for the legend, which sits on the top border line.
      default: 'border border-border pt-6',
      ghost: 'border-none bg-transparent'
    }
  },
  defaultVariants: {
    variant: 'default'
  }
});
export interface FieldsetProps
  extends React.ComponentProps<typeof BaseFieldset.Root>,
    VariantProps<typeof fieldsetVariants> {}
export function Fieldset({ className, variant, ...props }: FieldsetProps) {
  return <BaseFieldset.Root className={cn(fieldsetVariants({ variant }), 'rounded-surface', className)} {...props} />;
}
/**
 * Sits astride the fieldset's top border, interrupting it — the native `<legend>`
 * look. Base UI renders this part as a `<div>`, and a `<div>` gets none of the
 * browser's legend behaviour, so the effect is built here: pull it up onto the
 * border line and paint the page background behind it to punch out the gap.
 *
 * The background must match whatever the fieldset sits on. Override it (e.g.
 * `className="bg-card"`) when the surface underneath isn't `--background`.
 */
export function FieldsetLegend({ className, ...props }: React.ComponentProps<typeof BaseFieldset.Legend>) {
  return (
    <BaseFieldset.Legend
      className={cn(
        'absolute -top-[0.6875rem] left-3 bg-background px-1.5',
        'text-sm font-semibold uppercase tracking-[0.04em] text-foreground',
        className
      )}
      {...props}
    />
  );
}
export { fieldsetVariants };
````

## Menu (`menu`)

Menu built on Base UI.

- Type: `registry:ui`
- Install: `npx @ternetin/ui add menu`
- npm dependencies: `@base-ui/react@^1.9.0`
- Registry dependencies: `utils`, `motion`

### `src/ui/menu.tsx`

````tsx
'use client';
import { Menu as BaseMenu } from '@base-ui/react/menu';
import type * as React from 'react';
import { useMotionPopupRender } from '@/lib/motion';
import { cn, NESTED_RADIUS } from '@/lib/utils';
export const Menu = BaseMenu.Root;
export const MenuTrigger = BaseMenu.Trigger;
export const MenuGroup = BaseMenu.Group;
export const SubmenuRoot = BaseMenu.SubmenuRoot;
export function MenuContent({
  className,
  children,
  sideOffset = 6,
  style,
  ...props
}: React.ComponentProps<typeof BaseMenu.Popup> & {
  sideOffset?: number;
}) {
  const renderPopup = useMotionPopupRender();
  return (
    <BaseMenu.Portal>
      <BaseMenu.Positioner sideOffset={sideOffset} className="z-50 outline-none">
        <BaseMenu.Popup
          style={style}
          className={cn(
            'min-w-40 border border-border bg-popover p-1 text-popover-foreground shadow-popup outline-none',
            // Unfold from the trigger's edge instead of the popup's centre.
            '[transform-origin:var(--transform-origin)]',
            'rounded-surface',
            className
          )}
          render={renderPopup}
          {...props}
        >
          {children}
        </BaseMenu.Popup>
      </BaseMenu.Positioner>
    </BaseMenu.Portal>
  );
}
const itemClasses = cn(
  'flex cursor-pointer select-none items-center gap-2 px-3 py-1.5 text-sm leading-5 outline-none',
  NESTED_RADIUS,
  'data-[highlighted]:bg-accent data-[highlighted]:text-accent-foreground',
  'data-[disabled]:pointer-events-none data-[disabled]:opacity-40'
);
export function MenuItem({ className, ...props }: React.ComponentProps<typeof BaseMenu.Item>) {
  return <BaseMenu.Item className={cn(itemClasses, className)} {...props} />;
}
export function MenuGroupLabel({ className, ...props }: React.ComponentProps<typeof BaseMenu.GroupLabel>) {
  return (
    <BaseMenu.GroupLabel
      className={cn('px-3 py-1.5 text-xs font-medium uppercase tracking-[0.08em] text-muted-foreground', className)}
      {...props}
    />
  );
}
export function MenuSeparator({ className, ...props }: React.ComponentProps<'div'>) {
  return <div className={cn('-mx-1 my-1 h-px bg-border', className)} {...props} />;
}
export function MenuSubmenuTrigger({
  className,
  children,
  ...props
}: React.ComponentProps<typeof BaseMenu.SubmenuTrigger>) {
  return (
    <BaseMenu.SubmenuTrigger className={cn(itemClasses, 'justify-between', className)} {...props}>
      {children}
      {/* Signals that this item opens a submenu rather than performing an action. */}
      <svg
        viewBox="0 0 16 16"
        className="size-3.5 shrink-0"
        fill="none"
        stroke="currentColor"
        strokeWidth={2}
        aria-hidden="true"
      >
        <path d="M6 4l4 4-4 4" />
      </svg>
    </BaseMenu.SubmenuTrigger>
  );
}
````
